A1.justification: Despite the changed title and extensive revision, both PDFs describe the same ConfTS research. All pages, including v1 Appendices A–E and v2 Appendices A–J, are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original calibration and ConfTS experiments on CIFAR-100, ImageNet and ImageNet-V2, including benchmark results and temperature analyses.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark experiments, additional calibration comparisons, ConfTr and SAPS evaluations, and ablation studies.

M1.justification: Section 4 replaces v1's coverage-dependent sign/sigmoid loss with the squared efficiency gap, (tau-S)^2. v2 also changes temperature optimization to use held-out validation data split between threshold estimation and loss computation, separately from final conformal calibration. These change the objective and fitting procedure, beyond renaming compactness gap to efficiency gap.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate image classification on CIFAR-100, ImageNet and ImageNet-V2, including calibration and testing on the latter distribution using ImageNet-pretrained models. The additional algorithms, architectures and ablations do not introduce another dataset, task or population.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated label-smoothing, mixup and Laplace-approximation calibration methods in Table 5. It also adds comparisons of ConfTr-trained models with and without ConfTS (Table 3), and SAPS with and without ConfTS (Tables 10–11). The entropy-minimization comparison in v1 Table 4 is removed.

E3.justification: v2 replaces shared temperature-fitting and conformal-calibration data with independent subsets and revises the Section 3 data splits. It specifies randomized APS/RAPS evaluation, adds SSCV and size/penalty sweeps, and adds ResNeXt configurations on CIFAR-100. ImageNet-V2 reporting contracts from six architectures and two error rates to four architectures at approximately 0.90 coverage.

E4.justification: v2 adds validation/conformal sample-size ablations, randomized versus non-randomized score ablations, conditional-coverage analysis, and RAPS/SAPS penalty sensitivity studies. The adaptiveness comparison changes from APS/RAPS with ResNet50 to APS with ResNet18/50. v1's entropy-minimization analysis and supplementary temperature/coverage plots in Figures 4–5 disappear.

E5.justification: Table 1's stated trial count increases from 10 to 20. v2 additionally specifies different seeds throughout and introduces two-sample t-test markers, described as using a 0.1 confidence level. The unexplained parenthesized quantities in v1 Table 2 are no longer displayed. These refine repetition and statistical reporting.

E6.justification: Many benchmark values are replaced and substantial new results are added. For example, ImageNet ResNet50 APS at alpha=0.1 changes from baseline/ConfTS sizes 9.06/2.92 to 9.062/4.791 in Table 2; the revised method and protocol prevent interpreting this as a same-setting performance decline. v2 adds SSCV, ConfTr, calibration and sensitivity results, while removing ImageNet-V2 alpha=0.05 results, including several unfavorable RAPS outcomes.

T1.justification: v1 Theorem 3.2's class-removal probability bound and Appendix E proof are replaced by Theorem 3.3's expected-set-size upper bound with new CDF assumptions and derivations in Appendix F.3. v2 adds Corollary 3.2 and supporting lemmas, while removing v1's conditional uniform-score lemma and Appendix A.1 label-order theorem/counterexample.

C1.justification: The central efficiency motivation remains, but v2 extends the adverse-calibration claim to training-time and Bayesian methods and adds main claims about improved conditional coverage and compatibility with ConfTr. Its theoretical contribution is redefined around expected prediction-set size, and the paper more explicitly confines its claims to adaptive conformal prediction.

C2.justification: v1 attributes vector-scaling coverage loss to label reordering; v2 withdraws this account and explains preserved exchangeability through held-out fitting. v2 also explains extremely small-temperature failures through finite-precision truncation, interprets randomized-score optimization failures, and explicitly limits applicability to exchangeable data in Section 7.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands implementation documentation: 100-epoch SGD training, momentum, weight decay, batch sizes, learning-rate schedule, TorchVision model provenance and RTX 4090 hardware. It also supplies ConfTr and calibration-method hyperparameters. These are mainly newly disclosed details; v1 does not establish corresponding earlier settings that would demonstrate training changes.

R1.justification: Section 6 substantially revises positioning around post-hoc versus training-time conformal methods, adding discussion of Einbinder, Correia and SAPS. v2 newly identifies Gupta et al. (2020) as closely related binary-classification work and positions this study as a multiclass extension. Several earlier outlier-detection and distribution-shift references are removed.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, theoretical explanation, method, experiments, related work and conclusion undergo extensive rewriting. The title changes to Delving into Temperature Scaling for Adaptive Conformal Prediction, terminology shifts from compactness to efficiency, metric descriptions move to Appendix A, and the appendices are substantially reorganized. Author and affiliation information also changes.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from two-column to single-column layout. v2 combines the temperature analyses into Figure 1, redraws the extreme-temperature panel, adds an SSCV chart and numerical-error illustration, and expands Figure 3 with sensitivity panels. Tables are added, removed and restructured, including the relocated and transposed ImageNet-V2 comparison.

improvement.justification: Separating temperature fitting from conformal calibration addresses a central weakness in v1's coverage rationale. The revised objective, score/split ablations and fuller implementation details substantially strengthen methodological credibility. These gains outweigh reduced ImageNet-V2 reporting, although important defects remain: v2 Appendix F.3 assumes positive CDF separation even at common endpoints, and Section 5.2 quotes a ViT APS size of 5.759 where Table 2 reports 9.050.
